title: weighted-hibernation-slo-aware-deprioritizer
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a SLO-aware weighted hibernation scheduler policy that deprioritizes low-tier requests during sustained tail latency; exposes config knobs and metrics; safe rollout with canary and quick rollback.
description:
Motivation: We observed repeated tail-latency spikes that are driven by low-priority background workloads (embeddings batch scoring, low-importance rerank requests) during sustained load windows. Existing load-shedding and circuit-breaker primitives are either too coarse (drop whole tenant traffic) or too reactive (oscillate on short bursts). This PR introduces a 'weighted hibernation' scheduler policy: it slows and temporarily 'hibernates' low-priority request classes using a time-decayed weight and hysteresis so latency SLOs for high-priority traffic are preserved without wholesale dropping.

What this change does (high level): Adds a scheduler policy implementation, metrics and dashboards, configuration knobs and runtime toggles, tests, and a small hotpatch manifest to allow emergency rollback. Key behaviors: (1) SLO-aware scoring: each request class reports a target P99/latency SLO and the scheduler computes a dynamic weight to reduce scheduling rate for classes exceeding their contribution to observed tail latency; (2) Hysteresis + decay window: when a class is hibernated we apply exponential decay so it ramps back gradually rather than sudden bursts; (3) Weighted hibernation is non-blocking for critical classes and configurable by tenant tag (tier/prod/staging).

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler implementation + unit tests - [x] Integration tests in local canary harness - [x] Metrics + dashboards (console) - [x] Config schema + documentation - [x] Rollout plan and k8s hotpatch for fast rollback

Migration/Rollout plan: Deploy behind a feature flag defaulting to off. Roll out to internal canary (10% of traffic) for 6 hours, monitor p50/p90/p99 and request drop rates. If stable, ramp to 50% then global. Quick rollback: the hotpatch manifest (deploy/k8s/weighted-hibernation-hotpatch.yaml) toggles the feature flag to off and reverts the scheduler binary to last-known-good.

Testing performed: local unit test suite for scheduler weight math, integration with batcher and KV cache; end-to-end load test in benchmark-lab with mixed-priority synthetic workload showing 25-40% reduction in P99 for high-priority requests under the same tail load. CI initially failed lint (naming) and a flaky test; both were addressed and CI passed on the second run.

Security/operational notes: No new external surface added. Metrics emitted include: rts.scheduler.hibernation_count, rts.scheduler.hibernation_duration_ms, rts.scheduler.weight_adjustments, rts.scheduler.hibernation_decays. Add these to existing SLO dashboards for alerting.

Related work: builds on ENG-2071 (SLO attribution telemetry) and ENG-2145 (priority tagging for tenant requests). Not a breaking change; defaults to off.
